title: United States federal government: Phase 56O Remediation Follow-Through
summary: GAO estimates that implementing open recommendations could produce $132 billion to $251 billion in measurable future financial benefits; the range is model-based, excludes many nonquantifiable benefits, and is not realized savings. Phase 56O decision: Publish the modeled range as bounded government-wide context with the method and realization limits attached.
key_findings: Exact record: GAO-26-108932 government-wide open-recommendation benefit model.
Status period: Open recommendations as of October 2025; report published May 2026.
Continuation rule: Reopen when GAO updates the model, publishes realized benefit attribution, or materially revises the open-recommendation inventory.
why_it_matters: The record exposes implementation throughput and remaining remediation workload without converting a portfolio into a performance rate.
ftfn_relevance: Keeps implemented, added, de-prioritized, current, modeled, and realized states distinct.
Attaches source, period, scope, limitation, remaining gap, and continuation rule.
evidence_limits: The $132 billion to $251 billion range is a modeled government-wide potential-benefit estimate as of October 2025. It is not a forecast, budget score, agency allocation, or realized saving, and actual benefits depend on whether, how, and when recommendations are implemented.
Recommendation-level implementation, attribution, timing, realized savings, nonfinancial outcomes, and agency-specific allocation of any benefit.
No ranking, composite, readiness score, performance rate, or causal claim is supported.
